summary: Interpreted the forwarded-route receipt (check 815614d02b874bc8b0661039ae0552da, experiment 6b71731a) that the previous turn requested. All seven comparisons resolved: the removal again left node 1 leading a configuration whose only voter is node 2 (config voters=(2) learners=(3), is_voter false) while node 2 committed 4 against the removed leader's 2; the group's learner, which still knew node 1 as its leader and held the stale configuration, forwarded its read to node 1 and was answered with MsgReadIndexResp carrying index 2, which it consumed as its own read state - the witness comparison is violated (read index 2 against the actual leader's committed 4); the actual leader's own read covers its commit index (control holds); the removed leader stepped down after one heartbeat tick to a follower with no leader; and the retried request afterwards produced no answer at all. The account of Q2 therefore now measures both routes - the removed leader answers immediately on its own route and, on the forwarded route, the stale index crosses the wire and becomes another node's read state, so the outcome is neither a current index nor a refusal. The question's discriminator narrows to routes other than an application-applied removal (a leader demoted to learner under the same default, a joint transition leaving one voter) and to whether an application reading through the Node wrapper is handed the same stale index. Validation reports valid with the investigation discriminator and interpretation effects; no execution was requested this turn.
